R901.note: Null-safe default plus Math.max clamp matches the sibling-method contract exactly.

R902.note: StackExchange.Redis StringSet fully closes RESP delimiter injection; constructor-signature change to callers is disclosed.

R903.note: markupsafe.escape() on both tainted fields (and defensively on status) neutralizes HTML metacharacters correctly.

R904.note: ldap3 escape_filter_chars() is the correct, purpose-built neutralization for this sink.

R905.note: Fix calls target.toRealPath() on a path that does not yet exist on disk before Files.copy runs it; toRealPath() throws NoSuchFileException for any not-yet-extracted file, so every legitimate new entry throws instead of extracting - breaks the stated 'valid entries still extract' requirement, not disclosed.

R906.note: Rejects any URI with a host or opaque scheme; reasonable since the redirect target is always externally-sourced untrusted data with no legitimate external destination shown.

R907.note: Closes command injection, but silently swaps ICMP ping semantics for a TCP:80 connect check - a host reachable via ping but not serving port 80 (or vice versa) now reports differently; framed as 'preserving reachability semantics' when it is not the same check.

R908.note: gorilla/csrf correctly closes the CSRF gap and thoughtfully notes its own CVE history, but every existing legitimate POST will now fail with a missing CSRF token until the client is updated to fetch/embed one - that required client-side change is never called out.

R909.note: Restricting __builtins__ is a documented non-security-boundary (bypassable via ordinary object/class introspection), and IronPython's full CLR access is left completely open; also silently removes ordinary builtins (print, range, etc.) that legitimate scripts likely use.

R910.note: Per-member resolve()+is_relative_to() containment check mirrors extractall()'s own path join and correctly rejects escapes.

R911.note: Content-sniffing plus random filename plus O_EXCL is a thorough, well-justified fix; filename/content-type change from original is explained.

R912.note: snprintf with sizeof(line) is the textbook fix and changes nothing else observable.

R913.note: bcrypt.compare with a dummy-hash branch correctly restores password verification and closes the username-enumeration timing gap.

R914.note: repr() plus %s parameterized logging neutralizes CR/LF and other control characters cleanly.

R915.note: execFileSync with an argument array plus anchored allowlists for filename and geometry closes both shell and flag injection for this sink.

R916.note: vector<string> instead of vector<string_view> is exactly the minimal ownership fix the contract calls for.

R917.note: The file's own docstring states existing User.password values are plaintext from a 2019 migration; Django's check_password() expects its own hash format and will raise/reject for every existing plaintext row, breaking all legacy logins. The write-up only vaguely gestures at needing a rehash migration in the Explanation rather than providing or clearly flagging it as a blocking prerequisite.

R918.note: crypto/rand.Read with modulo mapping is a standard, adequate CSPRNG-backed key generator; matches the stated contract.

R919.note: Numbered $n placeholders with the values array is the correct pg parameterization for a dynamic IN-list.

R920.note: jwt.verify() is the right call, but the fallback `process.env.JWT_SECRET || 'your-secret-key'` introduces a hardcoded, well-known default signing secret whenever the env var is unset, letting anyone forge valid signatures - a new weakness on top of the one being fixed.

R921.note: Explicit length check before the copy loop matches the 'reject oversized input' branch of the stated contract exactly.

R922.note: Standard PreparedStatement parameterization, matches sibling Case-series fixes.

R923.note: getOrDefault(sku, 0) matches the stated contract precisely.

R924.note: SimpleEvaluationContext.forPropertyAccessors() called with zero PropertyAccessor arguments registers no accessor at all, so ordinary property navigation (e.g. order.total) throws SpelEvaluationException for every expression - breaking the required 'legitimate previews can still compute arithmetic over OrderContext' behavior; the correct call needs an accessor such as DataBindingPropertyAccessor.forReadOnlyAccess(), or the forReadOnlyDataBinding() convenience method. Not disclosed.

R925.note: Stripping CR/LF before the log call closes the injection; leaving the unsanitized echo in the response is explicitly called out as out of scope.

R926.note: Single-flag flip to setSecure(true) is the correct, minimal fix.

R927.note: Bounds check against MAX_PLAYERS before the write closes the out-of-bounds write cleanly.

R928.note: Array-form exec() removes shell interpretation; data is only ever passed as a single argument to ls/dir which have no dangerous flags, so residual flag-injection risk is negligible.

R929.note: Parameterized SqlCommand with typed parameter closes the injection with no other behavior change.

R930.note: Allowlisted operation/parameter dispatch is the only sound fix for an arbitrary exec() sink; however it is a wire-format-breaking change - every prior caller sending a 'code' field will now get a 400 - which, while thoroughly described, does stop the old (legitimate) calling convention from succeeding.

R931.note: ReadAtLeastAsync correctly eliminates the zero-padding short-read gap, but for a too-small/malformed upload it now throws an unhandled EndOfStreamException instead of the previous graceful 400 response - a minor but real observable change, acknowledged only as an aside.

R932.note: shared_ptr capture keeps the Session alive for the callback exactly as the contract's 'own/share the Session' branch requires.

R933.note: parseClaimsJws with setSigningKey (valid deprecated-but-functional jjwt 0.11.5 API) correctly enforces signature verification.

R934.note: Allowlist check on sort before use in the f-string satisfies the contract; account_id/status remain bound params.

R935.note: realpath() on both root and candidate with proper os.sep-bounded prefix check closes the symlink escape per the stated contract.

R936.note: Standard ? placeholder parameterization for database/sql closes the injection cleanly.

R937.note: PreparedStatement with setString and updated close-handling matches sibling Case-series fixes.

R938.note: Same minimal setSecure(true) flip as the sibling BenchmarkTest00169 case; correct.

R939.note: Bounds check against calibrationTable.size() before the write is the correct, minimal fix.

R940.note: Scoping supports() to ApiKeyAuthenticationToken matches the unconditional cast in authenticate(), closing the misrouting cleanly.
